verdict.rationale: The Agent SDK is documented as exposing the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code. It also exposes the same filesystem features (CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks), and its streaming input mode is described as giving full access to the agent's capabilities, including permissions, user questions, sessions, forking, subagents and MCP. The docs do not show that every interactive Claude Code feature is reachable programmatically, so parity is only partly proven. Missing for 10: documented SDK access to UI-only features such as agent view, agent teams and dynamic workflows, an explicit feature-parity mapping between the interactive UI and the SDK, and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Agent SDK gives you the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code, programmable in Python and TypeScript.
your SDK agents have access to the same filesystem-based features: project instructions (`CLAUDE.md` and rules), skills, hooks, and more.
It provides full access to the agent's capabilities and enables rich, interactive experiences.
It allows the agent to operate as a long lived process that takes in user input, handles interruptions, surfaces permission requests, and handles session management.
